results.title: Manhyia South MP allowed to retrieve passport as court varies bail terms
results.content: The High Court in Accra has varied the bail conditions of Manhyia South Member of Parliament, Nana Agyei Baffour Awuah, allowing him to retrieve his passport from the court registry. The Commercial Court 5 Division granted the application on Thursday, November 12, 2026, during proceedings in the MP’s trial over allegations of causing financial loss to the state and money laundering. His lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea, urged the court to approve the request, arguing that his client had no intention of fleeing the country. He also cited parliamentary rules requiring MPs to attend sittings, warning that prolonged absence without the Speaker’s written permission and a reasonable explanation could put the legislator’s seat at risk.

results.title: Health Ministry warns public against fraudulent Mercy Ships fundraising campaign
results.content: The Ministry of Health has warned the public against a fraudulent fundraising campaign being aired on some Ghanaian television stations, which falsely solicits money from people seeking surgical treatment through Mercy Ships.

results.title: Akufo-Addo appointed head of ECOWAS observer mission for Nigeria’s 2027 elections
results.content: Former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo will lead a 200-member ECOWAS Election Observation Mission to Nigeria ahead of the country’s January 16, 2027, general elections.

results.title: When the outrage dies, who remembers the victims? – The Obuasi SHTS case and our troubling habit of forgetting the people behind the headlines
results.content: The speed at which victims of sexual abuse, especially children, can become less central to the public discussion of their experience once the outrage dies away is deeply troubling.

results.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation
results.content: Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia, the artificial intelligence chipmaker he co-founded, following reports of two extramarital relationships, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence. Nvidia’s board of directors announced on Thursday, November 12, that Huang’s departure as CEO and board member would take immediate effect. His resignation follows an investigation launched by the company after reports that he had an intimate relationship with a woman identified in media reports as Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International. US intelligence officials reportedly suspected Alice Huang of working for Chinese intelligence, raising concerns about whether the relationship could have exposed sensitive company or national security information.

results.title: Power expires. Friendships shouldn’t
results.content: There is something profoundly disturbing about people who occupy fixed-term public offices or privileged corporate positions and suddenly develop amnesia about the relationships that existed before their appointments. The phone numbers remain, but the friendships disappear. People who once shared ideas, dreams and ambitions are suddenly considered too ordinary to associate with. Friends in entrepreneurship are ignored. Calls go unanswered. Requests for modest assistance are treated as personal inconveniences. Some even become unnecessarily arrogant, as though their appointments have permanently elevated them into another species.

results.title: UEW partners universities in Togo, Côte d’Ivoire and Benin on PhD training and research
results.content: The University of Education, Winneba (UEW), is pursuing stronger academic collaboration with three West African universities to promote joint supervision of doctoral students, research development and language proficiency programmes.

results.title: ‘The cedi knows no political parties’ – Mahama calls for collective responsibility
results.content: President John Dramani Mahama has called on Ghanaians to put aside political differences and take collective responsibility for protecting the cedi, insisting that the national currency belongs to everyone and should be valued beyond party lines.

results.title: Health Ministry warns against fake fundraising campaign targeting Mercy Ships patients
results.content: The Ministry of Health has warned the public against a fraudulent fundraising campaign being aired on some television stations in Ghana, which falsely claims to be raising money to support patients seeking free surgical treatment through Mercy Ships.

results.title: Lack of funding makes PhD sponsorship difficult in Ghanaian universities – UEW VC
results.content: The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), Professor Stephen John Mitchual, has raised concerns about funding constraints facing doctoral programmes in Ghanaian universities, saying the situation is making it difficult to secure sponsorship for PhD students.

results.title: Film Development Fund receives nearly 100 applications
results.content: The National Film Authority’s Film Development Fund has attracted nearly 100 applications seeking almost GH¢100 million, as 56 applicants enter the final stage of pitching.

results.title: What is ‘new economy’? Kwesi Pratt questions status of 24-hour economy promise
results.content: Veteran journalist Kwesi Pratt Jnr. has criticised the Mahama government’s “New Economy” slogan, demanding to know what it means and whether it signals the quiet abandonment of the 24-Hour Economy promise that brought the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to power. Speaking on Metro TV’s Good Morning Ghana on November 11, 2026, a day before Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson presents the 2027 Budget, Pratt questioned the sudden rebranding of the government’s economic agenda.

results.title: Africa needs $4bn yearly to expand clean cooking access by 2030 – Samira Bawumia
results.content: Former Second Lady Hajia Samira Bawumia has called for an annual investment of about US$4 billion to accelerate Africa’s transition to clean cooking, warning that inadequate funding is worsening health risks, deforestation and gender inequalities. She said the continent’s continued reliance on firewood and other traditional cooking fuels was undermining public health, environmental sustainability and the economic empowerment of women and girls. Speaking as a panellist at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Hajia Bawumia urged African governments, development partners and private-sector investors to make clean cooking a priority in the continent’s development and climate agenda. Citing estimates by the International Energy Agency (IEA), she said Africa required about US$4 billion annually to accelerate the adoption of cleaner cooking technologies

results.title: UKGCC mobilises corporate, public support to strengthen neonatal care at PMLCH
results.content: Speaking during the presentation ceremony to PMLCH, Adjoba Kyiamah, Executive Director of the UKGCC, shared the strategic vision behind the initiative, emphasising that marking a decade of trade facilitation and investment required leaving an indelible, life-saving imprint on the host community.

results.title: GHIB partners with property specialists to connect African clients with London residential developments
results.content: Ghana International Bank plc (GHIB) has announced a collaboration with Daniel Ford International and the Berkeley Group to provide African clients with information on selected residential developments in London, alongside access to the bank’s UK banking services. The initiative was unveiled at an event in Accra, targeting high-net-worth individuals, entrepreneurs, business owners and senior executives across the continent who have international banking needs. Through the collaboration, prospective property buyers can access information on selected residential developments within the Berkeley Group’s portfolio, with property advisory services provided by Daniel Ford International. GHIB said its role would be limited to providing banking services to eligible customers and would not extend to recommending, advising on, arranging or endorsing any particular property purchase. results.title: NAIMOS says personnel acted in self-defence during Manso Keniago clash that left six dead
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says the deaths recorded during Wednesday's confrontation at Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region resulted from an act of self-defence by its personnel.

results.title: Take a look at the new Ghana cedi notes introduced by the Bank of Ghana
results.content: The Bank of Ghana has introduced upgraded Ghana cedi banknotes with enhanced security features, improved durability, and more convenient, portable sizes.

results.title: GIPA CEO challenges private sector to demand accountability from public institutions
results.content: According to him, businesses should not tolerate unnecessary bureaucratic delays, particularly when they have fulfilled all the requirements for services to be delivered within stipulated timelines.

results.title: Government may turn to alternative bitumen suppliers if GoEnergy fails to deliver – Agbodza
results.content: The Minister of Roads and Highways, Governs Kwame Agbodza, has urged GoEnergy Company Limited (GOE), a wholly owned subsidiary of Goil Plc, to ensure a consistent and timely supply of bitumen to road contractors to help prevent shortages of the critical construction material from delaying projects.

results.title: Beauty Narteh elected first African woman to co-chair global anti-corruption coalition
results.content: The Executive Secretary of the Ghana Anti-Corruption Coalition (GACC), Beauty Emefa Narteh, has been elected Co-Chair of the Global Civil Society Coalition for the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), becoming the first African woman to occupy the position.

results.title: African climate groups call for equitable transition away from fossil fuels at COP31
results.content: African civil society organisations under the Pan African Climate Justice Alliance (PACJA) have called for a just, orderly and equitable global transition away from fossil fuels, as conversations about the roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels take shape at COP31.

results.title: BoG to roll out nationwide sensitisation campaign on new Heritage Series banknotes
results.content: The Bank of Ghana (BoG) is set to embark on a nationwide public education campaign to familiarise Ghanaians with the newly introduced Heritage Series banknotes and their enhanced security features.

results.title: Tensions rise in Manso Keniago as angry youth confront chief, accuse DCE over six deaths
results.content: Angry youth at Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region have besieged the palace of the paramount chief and nearly attacked the District Chief Executive (DCE) following the deadly confrontation involving residents, suspected illegal miners and personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS).

results.title: Eni Ghana pledges more opportunities for local firms in upstream sector
results.content: The Managing Director of Eni Ghana, Mr Federico Ricco, has reaffirmed the company’s commitment to strengthening local content development and expanding opportunities for local businesses in the country’s upstream petroleum industry. Speaking at the 2026 Local Content Conference and Exhibition in Takoradi, Mr Ricco said Eni’s experience with the Offshore Cape Three Points (OCTP) project demonstrated the value of combining international investment with a strong commitment to developing local capabilities.

results.title: Manso Keniago clash death toll rises to six, 15 injured
results.content: The death toll from the confrontation between residents of Manso Keniago in the Amansie South District of the Ashanti Region and personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has risen to six, with 15 others injured.

results.title: Galamsey would be worse without NAIMOS operations — Paa Kwesi Schandorf
results.content: The Spokesperson for the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), Paa Kwesi Schandorf, has defended the impact of the government's anti-galamsey operations, insisting that illegal mining would have reached far more devastating levels in Ghana if the task force did not exist.

results.title: AMA, KoKMA begin operations to clear traders from bus stops ahead of Christmas
results.content: The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA), in collaboration with the Korle Klottey Municipal Assembly (KoKMA), has begun an enforcement exercise to clear traders occupying bus stops in parts of Accra ahead of the Christmas festivities.

results.content: Two children have reportedly lost their lives after a passenger bus plunged into a roadside ditch at Kwameprakrom along the Ayanfuri-Dunkwa-on-Offin road.
